newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian officer killed by mine in Georgia.
newsitem.headline: Russian officer killed by mine in Georgia.

text.p: A Russian army officer was killed and two other servicemen were badly wounded when an armoured car carrying peacekeeping troops hit a mine in Georgia's breakaway Abkhazia region, a Defence Ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.

The spokesman gave no details, but Interfax news agency said the incident occurred on Monday in the Gali region, where Russian troops control a buffer zone separating Georgia from its Black Sea province of Abkhazia.
Abkhazia has run itself as a de facto independent state since driving Georgian forces out in 1993.

There was no immediate reaction from the Georgian capital, Tbilisi, but an Abkhaz security official called it a "terrorist act aimed at disrupting the peacekeeping operation". He blamed "a sabotage group" from Georgia.
Several Russian servicemen have been injured in similar incidents which both conflicting sides blamed on each other.
The explosion took place one day after a Russian sergeant shot dead 10 of his fellow servicemen in a peacekeeping unit in the Gali region and then killed himself.
The role of the Russian peacekeepers has become a heatedly discussed issue in Georgia recently.

The Tbilisi government is demanding that the 2,500 Russian peacekeepers patrolling the buffer zone take on a more aggressive mandate, helping refugees from the region resettle and expanding their area of activity.

The Georgian parliament passed a resolution last week seeking to end the Russian role in Abkhazia if no progress was made in bringing peace to the region by the end of their current mandate on August 1.
Sergei Yastrzhembsky, press secretary to Russian President Boris Yeltsin, called that "political blackmail".

He was quoted by Interfax news agency as saying the Georgian parliament was "forcing us to rethink the advisability of the further presence of Russian peacekeepers in the conflict zone and the possibility of fulfilling their mandate."
Observers say the departure of the peacekeepers could pave the way for a renewal of fighting between the separatists and Georgian government forces.
Nearly four years of peace talks have reached a dead end.
Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze last week offered a new start to peace negotiations, while ruling out any solution that recognised Abkhazia's independence.
But next day he also warned the separatists that they would be committing suicide if they chose to go to war again with a rebuilt Georgian army.
